adds.title: Human Rights Watch - March 2016 report urging decriminalisation
adds.summary: Tunisia Penal Code article 230 criminalizes sodomy with up to three years imprisonment and was enforced in September 2015 in Sousse where a 22-year-old was sentenced to one year later reduced on December 17 to two months served plus 300-dinar fine based in part on a forced anal examination finding compatibility with anal penetration, and on December 4-10 2015 in Kairouan-Rakkada where six students arrested after police found dresses and high heels in their apartment were sentenced on December 10 to three years plus three-year banishment from Kairouan later reduced on March 3 2016 to one month served plus 400-dinar fine with banishment quashed, with those detained subjected to beatings, demeaning remarks, and forced anal examinations used as proof of conduct, while Shams, an association supporting sexual and gender minorities, was suspended on January 4 2016 for 30 days after condemning the prosecutions with the suspension lifted on February 23.
